content: Cognitive capacity should be evaluated regularly in individuals with diabetes, particularly in those who have documented cognitive impairments or in older adults who are at an increased risk of cognitive decline. Cognitive functions, including attention, memory, logical reasoning, and problem-solving, are critical for effective self-management of diabetes. Cognitive decline is frequently observed in individuals with type 1 diabetes over prolonged periods and can significantly impair their ability to adhere to self-care routines, manage medications appropriately, and maintain optimal blood glucose control. Factors such as recurrent episodes of hypoglycemia, long-standing diabetes, and vascular complications contribute to an elevated risk of cognitive dysfunction. For individuals experiencing cognitive decline, healthcare providers should modify diabetes management plans to accommodate these changes. This may involve integrating support from family members or caregivers to assist with self-care tasks and ensure effective disease management.
